beats.text: Before you train your next model, see how DoSA cuts 2.74x of memory overhead.
beats.visual_focus: A dense matrix of glowing nodes suddenly dimming to a few bright points.

beats.text: The villain is the Brute-Force Dot Product. It treats every key like a VIP, forcing the GPU to score millions of useless candidates.
beats.visual_focus: A frantic bouncer checking IDs in a massive, endless line.

beats.text: DoSA shatters this by using Seed-Bound Pruning. We use a small, fast subset of keys to establish a winning threshold immediately.
beats.visual_focus: A threshold line cutting through a data cloud, instantly isolating the top candidates.

beats.text: We use vector magnitude bounds to reject candidates early. If a key's maximum possible contribution is lower than our seed, we skip it entirely.

feynman_certification.listener_verdict: The hook was solid—calling out the waste in attention mechanisms immediately resonated because I've dealt with O(n^2) bottlenecks before. I didn't cringe at any 'safe drawer' metaphors, which is a huge plus. My only issue is that 'Seed-Bound Pruning' sounds like a buzzword until you explain the magnitude check in Beat 4. Once you explained the magnitude check, it clicked, but the term itself felt a bit like jargon until the context caught up.

thriller_metadata.physical_analogy: A bouncer checking every single person in a city to find one VIP, instead of just checking the guest list.
thriller_metadata.paradigm_shift: Exact attention results without the exhaustive scoring tax.
